transcript.en: Hello English learners and welcome to EnglishPod.
transcript.zh: 大家好，英语学习者们，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

transcript.en: My name is Marco.
I'm Amira.
All right, Amira is here today and she is going to tell us about the wonderful lesson she has prepared this time.
transcript.zh: 好的，阿米拉今天在这里，她要给我们讲讲她这次准备的精彩课程。

transcript.en: Well, thank you, Marco.
Well, today we have a very interesting lesson prepared for you.
transcript.zh: 嗯，今天我们为大家准备了一节非常有趣的课。

transcript.en: It's about someone cutting in line.
Cutting in line, okay.
Yeah, it happens all the time and we all get very upset about it but, you know, it happens.
transcript.zh: 是啊，这种事经常发生，我们都会很生气，但是，你知道，它就是会发生。

transcript.en: Right, right.
Well, I imagine that everyone is wondering what cutting in line is.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我想大家都在想插队是什么意思。

transcript.en: Why don't we just listen to the dialogue one time and then when we come back Amira and I will gladly explain all the vocabulary in this dialogue.
transcript.zh: 不如我们先听一遍对话，回来后阿米拉和我会很乐意解释对话中的所有词汇。

transcript.en: Let's listen.
I can't believe it took us two hours to get here.
transcript.zh: 真不敢相信我们花了两个小时才到这里。

transcript.en: The traffic in New York is unbelievable.
transcript.zh: 纽约的交通简直令人难以置信。

transcript.en: Yeah, but just relax honey.
transcript.zh: 是啊，不过放轻松，亲爱的。

transcript.en: We're here and we're going on vacation.
transcript.zh: 我们到了，我们要去度假了。

transcript.en: In a few hours we'll be in Hawaii and you'll be on the golf course.
transcript.zh: 再过几个小时我们就到夏威夷了，你就可以去打高尔夫了。

transcript.en: Oh no, look at that line.
It must be a mile long.
There's no way I'm waiting for another two hours.
transcript.zh: 我绝不可能再等两个小时。

transcript.en: Honey, don't.
Hey man, the end of the line is over there.
Yeah.
No, seriously, I was here first and you can't cut in line like this.
transcript.zh: 不是开玩笑的，我先来的，你不能这样插队。

transcript.en: Says who?
I do.
So sue me.
Alright, that's it.
Whoa, I think there's punching.
transcript.zh: 哇哦，我想有人在打架了。

transcript.en: Yeah, I guess this guy was just a crazy, I don't know, impatient man, huh?
transcript.zh: 是啊，我猜这家伙就是个疯狂的、没耐心的人吧？

transcript.en: Yes, yes, but we don't want to talk about this now.
transcript.zh: 是的，是的，不过我们现在不想谈这个。

transcript.en: But for now, we will treat some of the vocabulary and very useful phrases in the dialogue.
transcript.zh: 现在，我们先来讲对话中一些词汇和非常有用的短语。

transcript.en: Great.
So, Marco, do you want to start?
Yes.
Let's take a look at our first word would be unbelievable.
transcript.zh: 我们来看第一个词，unbelievable（难以置信）。

transcript.en: Unbelievable.
Unbelievable.
Unbelievable.
Unbelievable.
Unbelievable.
Exactly, and just how you say it, it's something incredible, something amazing.
transcript.zh: 没错，正像你说的那样，它表示某事令人难以置信，令人惊奇。

transcript.en: Yeah, but I would like to point out that unbelievable was used here to describe the man's frustration.
transcript.zh: 是的，但我想指出，这里用 unbelievable 是来描述那个男人的沮丧。

transcript.en: He's not happy about the traffic in New York.
transcript.zh: 他对纽约的交通感到不满。

transcript.en: Exactly.
Perfect.
Okay, in the next part, the woman, she's trying to calm and relax her husband.
transcript.zh: 好的，在下一部分，那个女人，她在试图安抚和放松她的丈夫。

transcript.en: And she says that they'll be in Hawaii in a few hours and you'll be on the golf course.
transcript.zh: 她说他们几个小时后就会在夏威夷了，他就可以打高尔夫了。

transcript.en: Right.
So, we'll be in Hawaii and you'll be on the golf course.
transcript.zh: 所以，we'll be in Hawaii and you'll be on the golf course。

transcript.en: Yes, we'll be in Hawaii and you'll be on the golf course.
transcript.zh: 是的，我们会在夏威夷，你会在高尔夫球场上。

transcript.en: So, this is a great way of talking about your physical location in the future.
transcript.zh: 所以，这是一种很棒的方式来谈论你未来所在的实际位置。

transcript.en: Right.
So, for example, Amira, tomorrow where will you be?
transcript.zh: 那么，例如，阿米拉，明天你会在哪里？

transcript.en: Don't worry, Marco, I'll be in the office tomorrow.
transcript.zh: 别担心，马可，我明天会在办公室。

transcript.en: Perfect, right?
That's where I need you to be.
transcript.zh: 这就是我需要你在的地方。

transcript.en: Yes.
Okay.
All right, well, I have another interesting phrase here for you.
transcript.zh: 好了，嗯，我这还有一个有趣的短语。

transcript.en: Must be a mile long.
transcript.zh: Must be a mile long（肯定有一英里长）。

transcript.en: A mile long.
A mile long.
A mile long.
Now, that's basically not a mile, it's not a kilometer long, but it's another way of saying that this line is really, really long.
transcript.zh: 现在，这基本上不是一英里，也不是一公里长，而是另一种说法，表示这条队真的非常非常长。

transcript.en: Right, it's just an exaggeration.
Now let's take a look at there's no way.
transcript.zh: 现在我们来看 there's no way（绝不可能）。

transcript.en: There's no way.
There's no way.
There's no way.
Perfect.
Let's listen to some other examples on how we use there's no way in a different situation and then we can come back and talk about it a little bit more.
transcript.zh: 我们来听几个其他例子，看看 there's no way 在不同场景中的用法，然后我们再回来多聊聊。

transcript.en: There's no way I can have those reports finished today.
transcript.zh: 我今天绝不可能完成那些报告。

transcript.en: The stadium is so crowded that there's no way we'll find a seat.
transcript.zh: 体育场太拥挤了，我们根本不可能找到座位。

transcript.en: Do you think Michael's going to buy that house?
transcript.zh: 你觉得迈克尔会买那栋房子吗？

transcript.en: There's no way he has enough money to buy it.
transcript.zh: 他绝对没有足够的钱买。

transcript.en: All right, everyone.
So there's no way is another way of saying it is impossible.
transcript.zh: 所以 there's no way 是 it is impossible（不可能）的另一种说法。

transcript.en: Exactly.
There's no way you should miss this podcast, right?
transcript.zh: 你绝不能错过这期播客，对吧？

transcript.en: Yes.
Well, I have another phrase for you as well.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我这还有一个短语给你。

transcript.en: Cut in line.
Cut in line.
Cut in line.
Cut in line.
Cut in line.
So again, we have some really good examples on how you could use this phrase in different situations.
transcript.zh: 同样，我们有一些很好的例子，展示这个短语在不同场景中的用法。

transcript.en: Let's listen to the examples and then we can come back and talk about it some more.
transcript.zh: 我们来听例子，然后回来继续聊。

transcript.en: Excuse me, I'm really late.
transcript.zh: 不好意思，我真的很赶时间。

transcript.en: Can I cut in line, please?
transcript.zh: 请问可以让我插个队吗？

transcript.en: I hate it when people cut in line at the bank.
transcript.zh: 我讨厌有人在银行插队。

transcript.en: It's so rude.
I think it's okay when a pregnant woman cuts in line.
transcript.zh: 我觉得孕妇插队是可以理解的。

transcript.en: All right, everyone.
Cut in line.
Right.
So from the examples, we can understand that it means when you are standing in line somewhere and somebody gets in front of you.
transcript.zh: 所以从这些例子我们可以理解，它的意思是当你在某处排队时，有人插到你前面。

transcript.en: Right.
I have another phrase for you here.
transcript.zh: 我这还有一个短语给你。

transcript.en: Sue me.
Sue me.
Sue me.
Sue me.
Okay.
Now, sue me is not a nice phrase.
transcript.zh: 现在，sue me 不是一个友好的短语。

transcript.en: If you hear that, you know you're in trouble.
transcript.zh: 如果你听到这句话，你就知道你有麻烦了。

transcript.en: Yeah, it's kind of rude, I guess, to say, sue me.
transcript.zh: 是啊，说 sue me 是有点粗鲁吧。

transcript.en: Right.
Well, it actually means like taking someone to court and asking for money because someone has harmed you in a way.
transcript.zh: 嗯，它实际上意思是把某人告上法庭并索要赔偿，因为某人以某种方式伤害了你。

transcript.en: I think that we should listen to the dialogue one more time and try to figure out why he used that phrase and if he's really going to take him to court.
transcript.zh: 我想我们应该再听一遍对话，试着弄清楚他为什么用那个短语，以及他是否真的要把他告上法庭。

transcript.en: I can't believe it took us two hours to get here.
transcript.zh: 真不敢相信我们花了两个小时才到这里。

transcript.en: The traffic in New York is unbelievable.
transcript.zh: 纽约的交通简直令人难以置信。

transcript.en: Yeah, but just relax, honey.
transcript.zh: 是啊，不过放轻松，亲爱的。

transcript.en: We're here and we're going on vacation.
transcript.zh: 我们到了，我们要去度假了。

transcript.en: In a few hours, we'll be in Hawaii and you'll be on the golf course.
transcript.zh: 再过几个小时，我们就到夏威夷了，你就可以去打高尔夫了。

transcript.en: Oh, no.
Look at that line.
It must be a mile long.
There's no way I'm waiting for another two hours.
transcript.zh: 我绝不可能再等两个小时。

transcript.en: Honey, don't.
Hey, man, the end of the line is over there.
Yeah.
No, seriously, I was here first and you can't cut in line like this.
transcript.zh: 不是开玩笑的，我先来的，你不能这样插队。

transcript.en: Says who?
I do.
So, sue me.
All right, that's it.
All right, we're back.
Now, this guy, when he says sue me, he's just being rude.
transcript.zh: 现在，这个家伙，当他说 sue me 的时候，他只是粗鲁而已。

transcript.en: I mean, he's just being kind of impolite and telling him, I don't care.
transcript.zh: 我的意思是，他只是有点不礼貌，在告诉他，我不在乎。

transcript.en: Right, exactly.
Like, you can't do anything about it.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Okay.
Today in the studio, we have a guest.
transcript.zh: 今天在录音室，我们有一位嘉宾。

transcript.en: Her name is Sarah and she's from England.
Hi there.
Hello.
All right.
So, we're going to be asking her a couple of questions and she'll be a frequent guest on our show, so you can expect to hear from her a lot.
transcript.zh: 那么，我们要问她几个问题，她会成为我们节目的常驻嘉宾，所以你可以期待经常听到她的声音。

transcript.en: Well, she didn't know that.
Yeah, it's a surprise.
She knows now.
Well, Sarah, our topic today is about jumping the queue.
transcript.zh: 嗯，莎拉，我们今天的主题是关于 jumping the queue。

transcript.en: Okay, Amira, wait.
What is this jump the queue?
It's the same as cut in line, but in British English.
transcript.zh: 跟 cut in line 一样，不过是英式英语的说法。

transcript.en: Ah, okay.
Yes, queuing is very important in England.
transcript.zh: 是的，排队在英国非常重要。

transcript.en: We're very proud of our queues.
transcript.zh: 我们对自己的排队文化非常自豪。

transcript.en: It's true.
So what would be the reaction of people if they cut in line?
transcript.zh: 那么如果有人插队，大家的反应会是什么？

transcript.en: I think we do take it very seriously.
transcript.zh: 我想我们确实非常认真对待这件事。

transcript.en: I'm laughing now, but it's quite serious.
transcript.zh: 我现在在笑，但这其实挺严肃的。

transcript.en: So you don't dump the queue.
If people jump in front of you, you get a little tuts and you shouldn't be doing that.
transcript.zh: 如果有人插到你前面，你会啧啧不满，你不应该那样做。

transcript.en: We make it very obvious.
So you say it out loud?
We would, you know, perhaps say something.
transcript.zh: 我们会的，你知道，也许会说什么。

transcript.en: And we have systems, you know, in London on the Metro, on the underground, you have to stand on the escalators on the right and queue, and you can't jump in front.
transcript.zh: 而且我们有制度，你知道，在伦敦的地铁上，在扶梯上你必须靠右站排队，你不能插到前面。

transcript.en: You have to walk on the left and queue on the right.
transcript.zh: 你必须在左边行走，在右边排队。

transcript.en: And it's all very serious.
There's rules and regulations.
Is there like a queue handbook that you have to read in high school and kind of take a test on?
transcript.zh: 有没有像排队手册这样的东西，你在高中时必须读，还得考试？

transcript.en: Perhaps there should be.
There should be, yeah.
Wow.
What about New York, Marco?
Well, no, definitely, I guess this dialogue is similar to a reality of New York.
transcript.zh: 嗯，不，绝对没有。我猜这段对话跟纽约的现实很像。

transcript.en: If somebody gets in front of you or cuts the line, somebody is going to say something and probably end up in a fight if the guy is rude.
transcript.zh: 如果有人插到你前面或插队，肯定会有人说些什么，如果那人态度粗鲁，很可能最后会打起来。

transcript.en: Yeah.
Oh my God.
Yeah.
Well, Sarah, why don't you tell us, is there a line or a queue for almost everything in England?
transcript.zh: 嗯，莎拉，不如你告诉我们，在英国是不是几乎什么事都要排队？

transcript.en: It seems like we do just like to form a queue.
transcript.zh: 好像我们确实就是喜欢排队。

transcript.en: Yeah.
So, you know.
Can you think of like some other examples of where you would normally you wouldn't queue, but you do?
transcript.zh: 你能想到一些通常你不会排队但你却排队了的例子吗？

transcript.en: Oh, gosh.
Things like in the supermarket when you're trying to find some vegetables or something, I'd never push, I'd never sort of reach around or anything.
transcript.zh: 比如在超市里当你想找些蔬菜什么的，我绝不会推挤，绝不会伸手绕过别人之类的。

transcript.en: I'd just wait until that person had finished picking up their stuff and then go in.
transcript.zh: 我会只是等到那个人拿完他们的东西，然后再过去。

transcript.en: So, just try and...
So if like five people want to buy oranges at the supermarket, then you have a little mini queue of five people waiting.
transcript.zh: 所以如果像五个人想在超市买橙子，那你们就会有一个五个人等的小型排队？

transcript.en: There's no sort of just shoving through to the front.
transcript.zh: 不会有直接挤到前面去这种事。

transcript.en: You just don't do that.
So you don't stick your hand out and grab like a tomato.
transcript.zh: 所以你不会伸出手去抓一个西红柿。

transcript.en: If you do, again, you would make sure that that person knows, oh, I'm sorry, I'm just in a hurry or whatever.
transcript.zh: 如果你这么做了，同样，你会确保那个人知道，哦，对不起，我只是有点赶时间什么的。

transcript.en: But yeah, it's just letting someone go before you.
transcript.zh: 但是，是的，就是让别人先走。

transcript.en: It's a courtesy, I think.
Okay.
It's quite important to us.
transcript.zh: 这对我们来说相当重要。

transcript.en: All right.
Well, thank you so much, Sarah.
It was a pleasure.
Yeah, we'll have you back very soon.
transcript.zh: 是啊，我们很快就会再请你来。

transcript.en: So, all right, we're out of time, but we'll be back tomorrow with another lesson.
transcript.zh: 那么，好了，我们时间到了，但明天我们会带来另一节课。

transcript.en: And be sure to visit our website.
transcript.zh: 一定要访问我们的网站。

transcript.en: Don't forget that EnglishPod.com has many, many resources and also a community of users and teachers that can help you answer questions and interact with you.
transcript.zh: 别忘了 EnglishPod.com 有很多很多资源，还有一个由用户和老师组成的社区，可以帮助你回答问题并跟你互动。

transcript.en: Yes.
And you should definitely leave your suggestions.
transcript.zh: 你一定要留下你的建议。

transcript.en: But for now, I wish you all well and bye.
transcript.zh: 但现在，祝大家一切顺利，再见。

dialogue.zh: A：真不敢相信我们花了两个小时才到这里。纽约的交通简直令人难以置信。

dialogue.en: B: Yeah, but just relax honey, we're here and we're going on vacation. In a few hours we'll be in Hawaii, and you'll be on the golf course.
dialogue.zh: B：是啊，但是放轻松亲爱的，我们到了，我们要去度假了。再过几个小时我们就到夏威夷了，你就可以去打高尔夫了。
